findings.reason: mlx5e_ipsec_remove_trailer() saves struct ipv6hdr *ipv6hdr = ipv6_hdr(skb) and struct iphdr *ipv4hdr = ip_hdr(skb) at lines 48-49, then calls pskb_trim(skb, skb->len - trailer_len) at line 61, and afterwards dereferences both stale pointers (ipv4hdr->tot_len write + ip_send_check(ipv4hdr) at 65-66, ipv6hdr->payload_len write at 67-68). Untrusted source: the skb is a network packet carrying an attacker-controlled ESP trailer length byte (plen read via skb_copy_bits at 56 drives trailer_len), and the header fields it overwrites come from the packet. Unsafe use: pskb_trim()->___pskb_trim() (net/core/skbuff.c:2721-2723) calls pskb_expand_head(skb,0,0,GFP_ATOMIC) whenever skb_cloned(skb); pskb_expand_head (net/core/skbuff.c:2285-2363) kmallocs a new head, memcpy's data, and frees/releases the old head (skb_free_head/skb_release_data), so ipv4hdr/ipv6hdr dangle and the post-trim writes go into freed slab memory (UAF write, plus stale-read of the old tot_len/payload_len). Counterevidence/limits: the reallocation only fires when the skb is cloned at trim time; the exact caller path (mlx5e IPsec software-crypto/esw handling of the xfrm skb) and a run-time KASAN confirmation were not re-verified in this session, hence medium confidence.
findings.conclusion: mlx5e_ipsec_remove_trailer keeps ipv6_hdr/ip_hdr pointers across pskb_trim, which frees the old head for a cloned skb, so the post-trim tot_len/payload_len writes hit freed memory (stale-pointer UAF write).

findings.reason: be_lancer_xmit_workarounds() captures struct vlan_ethhdr *veh = skb_vlan_eth_hdr(skb) at function entry (line 1124) and struct iphdr *ip = (struct iphdr *)ip_hdr(skb) at 1139, then calls pskb_trim(skb, eth_hdr_len + ntohs(ip->tot_len)) at 1141 with the attacker-influenced IPv4 tot_len (padded short frames, skb->len <= 60), and after the trim dereferences the stale veh at 1155-1156 (veh->h_vlan_proto == htons(ETH_P_8021Q)) to decide VLAN_SKIP_HW. Untrusted source: transmitted network skb whose IP header/tot_len are attacker-chosen. Unsafe use: pskb_trim()->___pskb_trim() (net/core/skbuff.c:2721-2723) calls pskb_expand_head() when skb_cloned(skb), and pskb_expand_head (net/core/skbuff.c:2285-2363) allocates a new data buffer and frees the old head, so the entry-time veh pointer dangles and the 1155 read is a slab use-after-free read that can also drive a wrong be_insert_vlan_in_pkt decision. Counterevidence/limits: requires a cloned (or otherwise reallocating) skb reaching ndo_start_xmit for this NIC; ip itself is only read before the trim, and no run-time reproduction was done.
findings.conclusion: be_lancer_xmit_workarounds captures veh from the skb head at entry and reads veh->h_vlan_proto after pskb_trim, which can free the old head for a cloned skb, giving a stale-pointer UAF read on short padded TX frames.

coverage_gaps: Plain `ptr = skb->data + off` derivations and bare skb_trim() (not pskb_trim) were not enumerated by the scanner/greps, so the net/appletalk/ddp.c skb_trim pattern documented for s01 in fact f002 was never verified in s04.
i40e_txrx.c:3050, ixgbe_main.c:9461 and mpls_iptunnel.c:108 flagged vhdr/ttl uses after skb_cow_head but were not read to a conclusion before the session finalize limit.

Only net/ and drivers/net/ were searched (per branch instructions); helper uses elsewhere (e.g., netfilter core, wireless stacks under drivers/net/wireless beyond grep hits) were triaged only through grep line counts, not full reads.
limitations: No build or KASAN harness was run; the head reallocation on each reported path is inferred from the skb_cloned() branch of ___pskb_trim (net/core/skbuff.c:2721-2723) and pskb_expand_head's alloc-copy-free of the old head (net/core/skbuff.c:2285-2363) rather than observed.
Both findings require a cloned skb at trim time; on common TX paths skbs may already be uncloned, in which case the stale pointer still aliases valid (unmodified) memory and the issue is latent.

The caller path of mlx5e_ipsec_remove_trailer (which mlx5e IPsec/esw TX or RX entry invokes it, and whether those skbs can be cloned) was not re-verified in the final pass, so reachability rests on the function's own code.

The function-extent scanner matches derivations only through named accessors/function calls and one-line statements, so multi-line pointer arithmetic derivations may have been missed; 33 flagged triples were triaged, not all 559 grep hits.
